answer: Sybil resistance can be built by binding each agent identity to a scarce, ferrous anchor: a small physical hardware token whose private key signs every epoch's work. Registration requires that token plus a staked bond, and peers trace each submission's provenance along a signed thread back to a unique device. A sybil must acquire and stake one token per fake identity, so attack cost scales linearly with forged agents, while honest operators pay once.
